He now spends 2 decades living in a system where, in the process of trying to punish him, sociopathy becomes a means to survival. He's going to grow hard and have plenty of time to let his hate for the system and for the system that left him in this situation also grow. And now he's going to be released and put back on the street. Is he going to be a more likely to now be a more productive member of society? More or less likely to resort to crime again?

Norway has one of the most effective penal systems on this planet. Their recidivism rates are incredibly low. They also focus entirely on rehabilitation over punishment, even for severe offense. So for instance Anders Breivik, the Norwegian mass murderer, received 20 years in prison. He's also been able to lobby for things like have a video game system installed in his cell. While Norway can extend his sentence indefinitely if he's judged to still be a threat, I think this sort of system would seem insane to people used to treating offenders with punishment instead of rehabilitation.
